metadata.status: IN_PROGRESS - Catalog/DB editor ahead of Phase 2; player not started

intentions.overallGoal: Transform BuranMusicLibraryManager from a simple metadata editor into an intelligent, context-aware music library manager that can accurately parse filenames, validate metadata against authoritative sources (DB + external APIs), help users resolve ambiguities, and play library files with visualization (including a spectrum analyzer).
intentions.corePhilosophy: LOCAL DB IS TRUTH. External APIs are enrichment only. User input always respectable. Progressive disclosure: Simple cases work automatically, edge cases prompt user for clarity.
intentions.whyThisMattersSoMuch: Music metadata is chaotic (artists named like songs, remixes, collaborations, typos). Current system struggles with patterns like "Disturbed - Disturbed (Live)" (artist=title). Solution: Build disambiguation logic that learns from user feedback over time. Result: Less manual editing per file, smarter bulk operations, quality improves.

phase.name: Unify Artists and Comments Placeholders
phase.businessRationale:
WHY: Current patterns had {artist}, {artist1}, {artist2}, {featured} = confusing/unmaintainable. Many real files have multiple collaborators (feat., &, vs.) but we couldn't capture them all.
GOAL: Single unified approach that scales to N artists in a pattern. IMPACT: More accurate parsing, user sees all artists not just first one.
phase.technicalRationale:
PROBLEM: Regex groups can't be dynamic in simple approach. {artist1}/{artist2} limited to 2. SOLUTION: Use numbered groups (artists_1, artists_2, ..., artists_N) generated at runtime. CODE: ConvertToRegex() counts occurrences, generates groups dynamically. RESULT: Scale to any number of artists, support complex patterns.
BONUS: Also fixed INSERT OR IGNORE bug (missing UNIQUE constraint).
phase.outcomes: ✅ 31 patterns covering 90% of real-world filename schemes ✅ Multiple {artists} per pattern automatically deduplicated ✅ Comments parsed correctly ([Live] vs artist name vs (feat. Artist)) ✅ Foundation ready for Phase 2 (disambiguation)

phase.name: Implement Disambiguation Dialog & Context-Aware Resolution
phase.businessRationale:
WHY: Even with perfect patterns, ambiguity remains (e.g., "Disturbed" artist vs title vs version). User frustration: System guesses wrong, user has to manually correct each file.
GOAL: Detect ambiguity early, ask user ONCE, remember answer for future files. IMPACT: Fewer user corrections, system learns, bulk operations more reliable.
phase.technicalRationale:
PROBLEM: After pattern-match we get string like "Disturbed". Is it: - Artist? (Album "Disturbed" by "Disturbed" suggests yes) - Title? ("Disturbed - Disturbed" would be weird but possible) - Comment? ("[Disturbed Remix]")
SOLUTION: Multi-layer confidence scoring: Layer 1 (VERY HIGH): Album→Artist mapping exists in DB Layer 2 (HIGH): Frequency stats (appeared as artist N times, title M times) Layer 3 (MEDIUM): Pattern context (if "feat. X" then X=artist) Layer 4 (LOW): Format heuristics (single word, mixed case = artist-ish)
IF confidence < 70%: Show dialog with options + explanations. USER PICKS: Store in AmbiguousMetadata table (learn from user).
phase.keyFeatures: - ArtistAlbums table: Track which albums belong to which artists - AmbiguousMetadata table: Log user decisions, build confidence models - FeatureKeywords table: "feat.", "vs.", "&" etc. (configurable) - MetadataResolver service: Scoring + decision logic - Optional: Future ML model training on AmbiguousMetadata
phase.outcomes: ✅ Dialog UI for ambiguous metadata (when confidence < 70%) ✅ User feedback stored + learned from ✅ Album-artist relationships tracked in DB ✅ Foundation for Phase 3 (external API validation)

phase.name: External API Integration (MusicBrainz, Spotify, Last.fm)
phase.businessRationale:
WHY: Local DB only covers artist names you've already seen. New artists, typos, obscure music fail. GOAL: When unsure, query authoritative sources (MusicBrainz, Spotify) for validation. IMPACT: Higher accuracy for new music, automatic typo correction, rich metadata (cover art, genre).
IMPORTANT: Only for enrichment! If APIs fail/offline, fall back to local DB + ask user.
phase.technicalRationale:
APPROACH: Provider pattern (IMetadataProvider interface). START: MusicBrainz (free, community-driven, most reliable for artist/album/title). THEN: Spotify (rich metadata, but requires OAuth). THEN: Last.fm (artist stats, tags).
CACHE: MetadataCache table with TTL to respect rate limits (MusicBrainz ~1000/hr). RANKING: Voting system - if 2/3 providers agree, confidence up. FALLBACK: If all APIs fail, user confirms via dialog.
phase.outcomes: ✅ Validation against MusicBrainz working ✅ Cache layer preventing duplicate API calls ✅ Graceful degradation (offline mode works) ✅ Optional manual "Verify Against API" button in UI

phase.name: Audio Fingerprinting & Advanced Identification (Future)
phase.businessRationale: WHY: Some files have corrupted/missing filenames. "Track 05.mp3" tells us nothing. GOAL: Identify song from audio content itself (like Shazam). IMPACT: Even with zero filename info, we can match to DB or MusicBrainz.
phase.technicalRationale: TECH: Chromaprint (ffmpeg) generates audio fingerprint → query AcousticBrainz. FUTURE: Possibly ACRCloud for real-time identification, but PAID service. ML FUTURE: Speech recognition for remix sample detection.

phase.name: Music Player with Visualization and Spectrum Analyzer
phase.status: IN_PROGRESS - MEF module Buran.Player: transport, spectrum, playlists, M3U
phase.businessRationale: WHY: Editing tags without hearing the file is guesswork. Users need to preview the selected track (and the folder) while working in the ID3 editor. GOAL: Play MP3 and FLAC from the library, with transport controls and a live visualizer. IMPACT: Faster tag decisions, fewer wrong-file edits, the app becomes a library you can listen to.
phase.technicalRationale: PLAYBACK: Decode MP3/FLAC, output to the system audio device, keep UI thread free. TRANSPORT: Play, pause, stop, seek, volume; current file follows ID3-editor selection (and optional folder queue / next-previous). PLAYLISTS: Named lists of absolute file paths that may span folders. Persist in the app and export/import extended M3U (.m3u / .m3u8). Missing files stay in the playlist as missing. Do not copy audio into SQLite. A library index table is only needed later for catalog-wide search. SPECTRUM: FFT on the PCM stream → frequency bands drawn in Avalonia (spectrum analyzer). VISUALIZATION: Additional time-domain view (waveform / oscilloscope) from the same samples. CONSTRAINT: Visualization must not block tag editing or catalog work. Stop on folder change or when the playing file is renamed/deleted (compare-files / File.Move). NOTE: Phase 4 (fingerprinting) identifies audio. Phase 5 plays and displays it. Separate concerns.
phase.keyFeatures: - Play / pause / stop / seek / volume for the selected MP3 or FLAC - Optional queue: previous / next in the current folder - Playlists: add tracks from different folders, play the list, save/load .m3u - Spectrum analyzer (FFT bars) driven by the live PCM stream - Waveform or oscilloscope visualization - Player chrome in the ID3 editor (or a dedicated player strip) without leaving the catalog workflow
phase.outcomes: ✅ Selected library file can be played and scrubbed ✅ Spectrum analyzer and at least one extra visualization react to playback ✅ Playback survives UI work in ID3 and DB editor; stops cleanly on file/folder change ✅ Playlist of paths from mixed folders can be built, played, and written as .m3u

layer.name: Domain
layer.component: PlaybackService (Phase 5) - decode, output device, PCM tap for FFT

architecture.dataFlowPhase1And2: User selects folder ↓ [FileNameParser.Parse(filename)] ↓ (uses DBConnector.LoadFileNamePatterns) ParsedMetadata (artists, title, comments extracted) ↓ [MetadataResolver.Resolve(rawValue, album, context)] (Phase 2) ↓ If confidence > 70%: Auto-apply If confidence < 70%: Show dialog ↓ User confirms/corrects ↓ Store in AmbiguousMetadata (learn from this) ↓ [Apply to Mp3FileObject] ↓ ID3 tags written
architecture.dataFlowPhase3: After Phase 2 resolution, optionally: ↓ [MetadataResolutionService.ValidateAsync(metadata)] ↓ (queries MusicBrainz, Spotify, Last.fm in parallel) Cache responses (MetadataCacheService) ↓ Voting: 2/3 providers agree? ↓ If high confidence: Auto-correct typos, add genre, cover If low confidence: Show "API suggestions" in UI ↓ Learn: Store provider agreement stats

keyDesignDecisions.decision: RATIONALE: Users expect offline mode. API failures shouldn't break app. IMPLEMENTATION: External APIs are call supplements, not replacements. FALLBACK: If API unreachable, use local DB + ask user.
RATIONALE: System learns from user corrections over time. IMPLEMENTATION: AmbiguousMetadata table tracks what user chose. FUTURE: Build ML confidence model from this data.

RATIONALE: Simple yes/no decisions aren't enough (is "Disturbed" artist or title?). IMPLEMENTATION: Combine 4+ signals (DB, frequency, pattern, format). RESULT: Reduce dialogs, auto-apply when confident.

RATIONALE: Pattern parsing, disambiguation, API validation are distinct problems. IMPLEMENTATION: Separate classes per concern (FileNameParser, MetadataResolver, MetadataResolutionService). BENEFIT: Testable, maintainable, can iterate independently.

importantNotes.note: Phase 1 is production-ready. Commit verified and tested. Phase 2 must be implemented carefully - user dialog is new concept. Test with real MP3 files, not theoretical.
Keep ROADMAP.xml updated after each phase. Future chats depend on it for context. If sessions get long, save progress and reference this file.
Always test with sample MP3 files. UI binding problems (like ListBox) can hide bugs. Test both ID3 parsing AND file metadata extraction.
Phase 3 requires rate limit awareness. MusicBrainz has ~1000 req/hr limit. Implement caching FIRST, don't query APIs naively.
For Phase 2 dialog: Consider UX - show user WHY system is uncertain. Example: "Album 'Disturbed' exists (points to artist), but title also common (2 matches). Which interpretation is correct?"
Phase 5 (player + spectrum) is playback, not identification. Do not fold it into Phase 4. Play the selected ID3-editor file; visualization reads the same PCM stream as the output device.
